# Setting Up Code from Previous Assignment

```{r}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(lubridate)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(baguette)
library(ranger)
library(ggplot2)

# ==========================================
# READ AND CLEAN DATA
# ==========================================

bike_data <- read_csv(
  "https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/datasets/SeoulBikeData.csv",
  locale = locale(encoding = "latin1")
)

# Check missing values
bike_data |>
  is.na() |>
  colSums()

# Check column types
attributes(bike_data)$spec

# Convert Date to date format
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  mutate(date = lubridate::dmy(Date)) |>
  select(-Date)

# Summary of variables
summary(bike_data)

# Check categorical variables
unique(bike_data$Seasons)
unique(bike_data$Holiday)
unique(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)

# Convert categorical variables to factors
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  mutate(
    seasons = factor(Seasons),
    holiday = factor(Holiday),
    fn_day = factor(`Functioning Day`)
  ) |>
  select(-Seasons, -Holiday, -`Functioning Day`)

# Rename variables
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  rename(
    bike_count = `Rented Bike Count`,
    hour = Hour,
    temp = `Temperature(°C)`,
    wind_speed = `Wind speed (m/s)`,
    humidity = `Humidity(%)`,
    vis = `Visibility (10m)`,
    dew_point_temp = `Dew point temperature(°C)`,
    solar_radiation = `Solar Radiation (MJ/m2)`,
    rainfall = `Rainfall(mm)`,
    snowfall = `Snowfall (cm)`
  )

# Remove non-functioning days
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  filter(fn_day == "Yes") |>
  select(-fn_day)

# Aggregate hourly data into daily observations
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  group_by(date, seasons, holiday) |>
  summarize(
    bike_count = sum(bike_count),
    temp = mean(temp),
    humidity = mean(humidity),
    wind_speed = mean(wind_speed),
    vis = mean(vis),
    dew_point_temp = mean(dew_point_temp),
    solar_radiation = mean(solar_radiation),
    rainfall = sum(rainfall),
    snowfall = sum(snowfall)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# View cleaned data
bike_data

# ==========================================
# EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS (EDA)
# ==========================================

# Overall summary statistics for bike_count
bike_data |>
  summarize(
    across(
      bike_count,
      .fns = c(
        mean = mean,
        median = median,
        sd = sd,
        IQR = IQR,
        min = min,
        max = max
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )
  )

# Summary statistics by holiday
bike_data |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarize(
    across(
      bike_count,
      .fns = c(
        mean = mean,
        median = median,
        sd = sd,
        IQR = IQR,
        min = min,
        max = max
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )
  )

# Summary statistics by season
bike_data |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarize(
    across(
      bike_count,
      .fns = c(
        mean = mean,
        median = median,
        sd = sd,
        IQR = IQR,
        min = min,
        max = max
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )
  )

# Summary statistics by season and holiday
bike_data |>
  group_by(seasons, holiday) |>
  summarize(
    across(
      bike_count,
      .fns = c(
        mean = mean,
        median = median,
        sd = sd,
        IQR = IQR,
        min = min,
        max = max
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )
  )

# Correlation matrix for numeric variables
bike_data |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  cor() |>
  round(3)

# Bike count vs temperature
ggplot(
  bike_data,
  aes(x = temp, y = bike_count)
) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = seasons)) +
  facet_grid(~holiday)

# Bike count vs solar radiation
ggplot(
  bike_data,
  aes(x = solar_radiation, y = bike_count)
) +
  geom_point(aes(color = seasons)) +
  facet_grid(~holiday)

```

# HW 10 - Modeling Practice

```{r}
# ==========================================
# HW 10: TRAIN / TEST SPLIT
# ==========================================

library(tidymodels)

set.seed(558)

bike_split <- initial_split(
  bike_data,
  prop = 0.75,
  strata = seasons
)

bike_train <- training(bike_split)
bike_test <- testing(bike_split)

# 10-fold cross-validation on training data
set.seed(11)

bike_folds <- vfold_cv(
  bike_train,
  v = 10,
  strata = seasons
)

# Main Effects
rec1 <- recipe(bike_count ~., data = bike_train) |>
  step_date(date, features = "dow", keep_original_cols = FALSE) |>
  step_mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
        "Weekend", "Weekday"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  step_rm(date_dow) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

# Recipe 2: Add Interactions
rec2 <- rec1 |>
  step_interact(
    terms = ~ starts_with("seasons_"):starts_with("holiday_") +
      starts_with("seasons_"):temp + temp:rainfall
  )

# Recipe 3: Add Quadratic Terms
rec3 <- rec2 |>
  step_mutate(
    temp_sq = temp^2,
    humidity_sq = humidity^2
  )

# Set up Linear Regression Model
lm_spec <- linear_reg() |>
  set_engine("lm")

# Create Workflows
wf1 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec1) |>
  add_model(lm_spec)

wf2 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec2) |>
  add_model(lm_spec)

wf3 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec3) |>
  add_model(lm_spec)

# Fit using 10-fold Cross-Validation
set.seed(558)

res1 <- fit_resamples(
  wf1,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

res2 <- fit_resamples(
  wf2,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

res3 <- fit_resamples(
  wf3,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

# Compare Cross-Validation Results
collect_metrics(res1)
collect_metrics(res2)
collect_metrics(res3)

# Combined RMSE comparison
mlr_results <- bind_rows(
  collect_metrics(res1) |> mutate(model = "Model 1"),
  collect_metrics(res2) |> mutate(model = "Model 2"),
  collect_metrics(res3) |> mutate(model = "Model 3"),
)

mlr_results |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)
```

Based on the 10-fold cross-validation results, Model 3 performed the best with the lowest RMSE of 3069.408 and MAE of 2323.075. This suggests that including the interaction and quadratic terms improves predictive performance compared with the simpler models. Model 3 was selected as the best multiple linear regression model.

## Fit the Best MLR Model using last_fit()

```{r}
# Final MLR Model: Model 3

final_mlr <- last_fit(
  wf3,
  split = bike_split,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

# View test set performance
collect_metrics(final_mlr)

# Extract final fitted workflow
final_mlr_wf <- extract_workflow(final_mlr)

# View coefficient table
final_mlr_wf |>
  extract_fit_parsnip() |>
  tidy()

# View full regression summary
final_mlr_wf |>
  extract_fit_parsnip() |>
  pluck("fit") |>
  summary()
```

The final model (model 3) achieved a test RMSE of 3059.349 and MAE of 2132.168. The training R-squared was 0.9231, indicating a strong fit of the training data.

## Fit a Tuned Regression Tree

```{r}
# Regression Tree
tree_spec <- decision_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune(),
  min_n = tune()
) |>
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")

# Create workflow using Recipe 1
tree_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec1) |>
  add_model(tree_spec)

# Create tuning grid
tree_grid <- grid_regular(
  cost_complexity(),
  tree_depth(),
  min_n(),
  levels = 3
)

# Tune using 10-fold cross-validation
set.seed(558)

tree_tune <- tune_grid(
  tree_wf,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  grid = tree_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

# View tuning results
collect_metrics(tree_tune)

# Select best tree based on RMSE
best_tree <- select_best(
  tree_tune,
  metric = "rmse"
)

best_tree

# Finalize workflow with best parameters
final_tree_wf <- finalize_workflow(
  tree_wf,
  best_tree
)

# Fit final tree on entire training set
final_tree_fit <- fit(
  final_tree_wf,
  data = bike_train
)

# Plot final regression tree
final_tree_fit |>
  extract_fit_engine() |>
  rpart.plot()
  
```

```{r}
bag_spec <- bag_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune(),
  min_n = tune()
) |>
  set_engine("rpart", times = 25) |>
  set_mode("regression")

# Create workflow using Recipe 1
bag_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(rec1) |>
  add_model(bag_spec)

# Create tuning grid
bag_grid <- grid_regular(
  cost_complexity(),
  tree_depth(),
  min_n(),
  levels = 3
)

# Tune using 10-fold cross-validation
set.seed(558)

bag_tune <- tune_grid(
  bag_wf,
  resamples = bike_folds,
  grid = bag_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae)
)

# View tuning results
collect_metrics(bag_tune)

# Select best bagged tree based on RMSE
best_bag <- select_best(
  bag_tune,
  metric = "rmse"
)

best_bag

# Finalize workflow
final_bag_wf <- finalize_workflow(
  bag_wf,
  best_bag
)

# Fit best bagged tree on entire training set
final_bag_fit <- fit(
  final_bag_wf,
  data = bike_train
)


```

The bagged tree model was tuned using 10-fold cross-validation. The best tuning parameters were a cost complexity of 3.162278e-06, tree depth of 15, and minimum node size of 2. The selected model was then fitted to the entire training dataset. Its predictive performance will be evaluated on the test set and compared with the other models.
